definitions.gloss: cold sweat; breaking out in a cold sweat
definitions.explanation: Perspiration caused by fear, anxiety, nervousness, or a close call rather than by heat or exertion.

examples.japanese: ⟦{危|あぶ}ない→危ない：00768_abunai⟧⟦ところ→ところ：01137_tokoro⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{冷汗|れいかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: I broke into a cold sweat at the close call.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{呼|よ}び{出|だ}された→呼び出す：04813_yobidasu⟧とき、{冷汗|れいかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まらなかった→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧。
examples.english: When I was called in by my boss, the cold sweat wouldn't stop.

notes:
Composed of {冷|れい} (cold) and {汗|かん} (sweat). The more colloquial form is ⟦{冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}→冷や汗：19109_hiyaase⟧ (ひやあせ), which is far more common in everyday speech. {冷汗|れいかん} tends to appear in written or more formal contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冷汗|れいかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かく: to break out in a cold sweat
- {冷汗|れいかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: cold sweat comes out
- {冷汗|れいかん}{三斗|さんと}: sweating profusely from fear (idiomatic)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}→冷や汗：19109_hiyaase⟧: cold sweat — the colloquial equivalent, much more common in speech
- ⟦{脂汗|あぶらあせ}→脂汗：24142_aburaase⟧: clammy/greasy sweat — sweat from extreme pain or distress
- ⟦{寝汗|ねあせ}→寝汗：08194_nease⟧: night sweat — perspiration during sleep

NOTE ON READINGS:
Do not confuse with ⟦{霊感|れいかん}→霊感：22214_reikan⟧ (spiritual sensitivity/inspiration), which is a homophone.
